problem: Humanoid loco-manipulation methods based on imitation of mocap or teleoperation demonstrations depend on privileged global robot and object state, follow fixed reference motions, and adapt poorly to failures such as slippage or drops. Vision-only pose estimates also fail under occlusion and limited field of view.
motivation: Real humanoid deployment needs fully onboard, autonomous navigation, lifting and delivery that recovers from failures. The paper's observation is that vision is mostly needed to initiate a grasp, while proprioception and action history can keep the object state during contact, so a recurrent estimator can be trained jointly with an RL policy.
key_idea: Jointly train an LSTM object-pose estimator (fusing intermittent vision, proprioception and actions) with a residual RL whole-body manipulation policy on top of a frozen locomotion policy, and use LiDAR odometry for navigation, all zero-shot sim-to-real.
insight: Estimated object pose from proprioceptive memory gets the policy close to Oracle (MuJoCo whole-task success 0.75 vs 0.79), while Pure RL + FK falls to 0.61 and imitation learning to 0.00, so the estimator helps most under sim-to-sim shift. The estimator error drops once the AprilTag is visible and stays low during carrying through contact-driven proprioception. RL also yields many regrasps (6.32 in MuJoCo), showing recovery behavior that a fixed reference motion lacks.
method: Base whole-body locomotion policy: PPO-trained policy for the Unitree G1 (29 DoF) that tracks velocity, yaw-rate and base-height commands, frozen afterwards; asymmetric actor-critic with a bilateral symmetry loss.

Residual manipulation policy: on top of the frozen base, outputs 4-D locomotion commands plus 17-D residual upper-body PD targets, with rewards for kinematic tracking, box stabilization, contact-force quality and slip avoidance; the critic gets privileged box state and contact forces.

Recurrent object state estimator: LSTM (hidden size 128) with an MLP head takes the vision pose (zeroed when unavailable), proprioception and the executed action, and outputs the 6D box pose in the robot frame; trained with supervised GT poses concurrently with RL.
Estimator-to-policy curriculum: the policy input is w*estimated + (1-w)*GT with w=min(t/T,1); training uses noisy, randomly masked GT pose instead of rendered vision.
LiDAR navigation and staging: FAST-LIO odometry drives navigation to the box; within 0.5 m the AprilTag vision pose is activated for grasping, lifting and delivery.
Domain randomization: base mass, friction, PD gains, disturbances, and box mass, scale, COM and friction/restitution.

setting.backbone: PPO-trained MLP policies (base locomotion + residual manipulation, [512,256,128]) plus an LSTM(128)+MLP state estimator, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Simulation RL in IsaacLab, roughly 1 day per policy on one RTX 4090; no demonstrations or teleoperation data
setting.observation: Onboard RealSense D435i RGB-D (AprilTag pose), Livox Mid-360 LiDAR (FAST-LIO odometry), and proprioception (joints, IMU)
setting.action_space: Velocity/height commands to a frozen locomotion policy plus residual upper-body joint position targets, via PD control at 50 Hz
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT pose only in the Oracle baseline and as training-time critic and supervision)

numbers.extra: AprilTag pose at evaluation; success rates given as fractions
trained in IsaacLab only, evaluated in MuJoCo without fine-tuning
numbers.evidence: Table sim-to-sim, MuJoCo AdaptManip row; text: 'AdaptManip achieved a 75% success rate'

numbers_note: Custom benchmark, not a standard navigation benchmark. The sim-to-sim table is duplicated in the source. Real-world results are qualitative only (no numeric success rate). Unseen-object results: cylinders 82±14 (X), 86±8 (Y), 78±11 (Z), sphere 51±21.
results: In unseen MuJoCo, AdaptManip reaches 75% whole-task success vs Oracle 79%, Pure RL + FK 61%, Pure RL 37% and IL 0%. In IsaacLab it reaches 85%, comparable to Pure RL + FK (88%) and above Pure RL (62%) and IL (42%). It transfers zero-shot to a real Unitree G1 with onboard sensing, including corrective regrasping.
limitations: Only box lifting is evaluated with a single AprilTag for vision; real-world results are qualitative with no success statistics.
Unarticulated rubber hands limit manipulation, and generalization to other shapes is weaker (sphere 51%).
In IsaacLab it does not beat Pure RL + FK (85 vs 88), so the estimator's benefit shows mainly under sim-to-sim shift.
builds_on: Legged Gym-style locomotion rewards (Rudin et al.)
